[ota-hal] OTA-1655: the card is asked, not read

Owner: "Run a comprehensive audit across all code, schema definitions, item
tables, and OTA updates deployed over the last 24 hours… make sure they all
work."

⚠ THE AUDIT'S ONE REPAIRABLE FINDING, AND HOW IT WAS FOUND. "Do the suites
pass?" is the wrong question — they all pass. The question that finds anything
is HOW each suite proves its OTA: assertions that CALL the code and check the
answer, versus assertions that read the source file and look for a string. All
twenty OTAs from the last day were scored that way:

  ota1634 25/26 behavioural   ota1644 27/28   ota1649 73/88
  ota1635 25/25               ota1645 24/24   ota1650 68/72
  ota1636 21/26               ota1646 34/39   ota1651  1/23  ⚠
  ota1637 28/38               ota1647 24/25   ota1652 20/22
  ota1638 24/36               ota1648 10/17   ota1653 21/27
  ota1639 15/16   ota1640 19/25   ota1641 16/17   ota1642 16/18   ota1643 53/53

Nineteen carry real proof. ⚠ OTA-1651 is the outlier at ONE, and it is the one
that moved what the player looks at: the enemy's flavour line and his own hands
off the combat card and into the expanded popup.

A source pin cannot tell a working card from a broken one. Rename a local and it
goes RED on correct code; route the same text through another helper and it
stays GREEN on a card that lost the line. Two of those pins are worse than that:
they compare `.indexOf` of two SOURCE strings to assert that the flavour prints
ABOVE the numbers — which measures the order two `lines.push` CALLS appear in the
file, not the order the lines come out.

`enemyDetailBody` was already pure — an EnemyView in, a block of text out, no
hooks, no state, no rendering — and module-local only because nothing had needed
it. So the whole fix is one export, and ota1655 asks the card what OTA-1651
promised:

  • the flavour is in the body, and above the HP line MEASURED ON THE RENDERED
    LINES rather than on the source
  • both hands are named in words — and the sentence still says what it means
    with the ●/○ glyphs stripped out, which is the entire reason they moved off
    the combat card
  • a flavourless enemy leaves no blank gap and never the word "undefined"
  • ⚠ an unreadable foe SAYS it is unreadable: a card that simply omitted the
    section would read as "this thing has no defences"
  • Wisdom 12 discloses exactly what the gate withheld, and what you have already
    SEEN shows through with the line telling you how to learn the rest
  • no enemy shape a save can hold — no flavour, no traits, no range, 0 HP —
    makes the popup throw, because a popup that throws takes the screen with it

⚠ ONE FIXTURE ASSUMPTION OF MINE WAS WRONG AND THE RUN CAUGHT IT: the first
draft handed the boss `weaknesses: ['burn']` and asserted Burn came back. It
does not — defences come from `defensesFor`, the OTA-1611 reconciler that reads
the enemy's type and traits, and no fixture can hand them over. The test now
asserts what is actually true and actually matters: a boss's defences are
DISCLOSED and each is named in words beside a labelled type, whatever those
types resolve to.

The rest of the audit is reported to the owner, not committed: recipes 205/205
resolve with 0 missing ingredients, 0 missing results and 0 duplicate
ingredients; shields sit at 150/200/265/350 by rarity in weapons.json with the
blow landing on the shield 100% of the time barring a best-of bypass trait;
dog vests and golem arms equip, wear, warn and repair; and no unguarded catalog
lookup, floating promise or unparsed JSON was found in the 47 TS/TSX files the
day touched.

Gates: all 18 green by exit code. Full suite green — 1118 suites, 11,562 tests.
